title: Red Enchilada Casserole
summary: Shredded chicken cooked right in a homemade red sauce, layered with black beans, charred corn, blended cottage cheese, and crisped melting cheese. The traditional version gets its fat from 80/20 beef, tortillas fried in oil, and a heavy hand with cheese and sour cream. Here the sauce doubles as the cooking liquid, the tortillas are warmed instead of fried, and the cheese is measured and mostly sits on top where it crisps. Fits a 9x13 dish.

builds.label: Beef eye of round
builds.note: Eye of round braised 2.5 to 3 hr in the same sauce in place of the chicken. Adds about 15 calories and 2g fat per serving and stays in the fat range. It shreds a bit drier, so the filling gets extra sauce.

builds.label: Beef chuck, trimmed
builds.note: Trimmed chuck braised 2.5 to 3 hr in the same sauce. Richer and closer to the traditional, but fat lands at 34%, above the target. Adds about 55 calories and 8g fat per serving for 3g less protein.

ingredients.raw: 1.5 lb beef chuck, trimmed of thick fat
1 can (15oz) yellow sweet kernel corn, no salt added, drained
1 jalapeño, diced (seeds in for heat, out for background warmth)
1 can (8oz) tomato sauce, no salt added
2 1/2 tbsp cornstarch + 1/2 cup cold water, for the slurry
1 tbsp adobo sauce from a can of chipotles (optional, adds smoky heat)
Chili powder 2 tbsp, cumin 2 tsp, smoked paprika 1 tsp, oregano 1 tsp, garlic powder 1 tsp, onion powder 1 tsp, cayenne 1/2 tsp, black pepper 1/2 tsp
Sweet paprika 1 tbsp, kept separate from the mix (it goes in with the liquids)
Salt, starting with 1 tsp and adjusting at the end (the cheese and beans already carry some)
1 tub (16 oz, about 2 cups) 2% cottage cheese, blended with 2 tbsp milk
5 oz (about 1 1/4 cups) shredded melting cheese: quesadilla cheese, Oaxaca, or asadero (macros land within a few calories of each other)
About 1 cup of the finished sauce, held back and kept warm to spoon over the cheese

steps.body: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
If braising in the oven, preheat it to 300°F.
Dice the onion, bell pepper, and jalapeño. Mince the garlic.
Mix the spice mix in a bowl. Keep the sweet paprika on the side.
Drain the beans and corn, patting the corn dry so it chars instead of steams. Char the corn in a dry hot pan, 4 to 6 min, leaving it alone between stirs until it has browned spots.
Cut any thick chicken breast in half horizontally so the pieces are an even 1 inch or a bit under. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the beef into 2 to 3 inch chunks, trimming any thick fat or silverskin. Season with salt and pepper.
Blend the cottage cheese and milk 30 to 60 sec until silky. Refrigerate.
Mix the cornstarch slurry.
Slice the scallions and cut the lime wedges.

Pickled jalapeños, if making them: stir the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt until dissolved (30 sec in the microwave helps) and pour over the sliced jalapeños in a jar. They need at least 30 min, so they're ready by the time the casserole comes out.
**Sweat the vegetables.** Heat the oil over medium. Cook the onion, bell pepper, and jalapeño 5 to 6 min until soft, adding the garlic for the last 30 sec.
**Bloom the spices.** Stir in the spice mix and tomato paste and cook 1 min, until it darkens and smells toasted. This takes the raw edge off the chili powder.

**Build the sauce.** Add the tomato sauce, broth, sweet paprika, brown sugar, and adobo if using. Stir until the paprika dissolves, then bring to a bare simmer. Paprika scorches fast in a dry pan, so it goes in with the liquid to stay red instead of turning brown.

**Poach the chicken.** Nestle the pieces in a single layer in the sauce, mostly submerged. Cover and hold at the lowest heat that keeps a few lazy bubbles breaking, 15 to 20 min, flipping once, until the thickest piece reads **165°F**.

**Braise the beef.** Nestle the chunks in the sauce, mostly submerged. Cover and hold at the lowest simmer on the stove, or move the covered pot to the 300°F oven, 2.5 to 3 hr, turning the pieces every 45 min, until they shred easily with a fork. If the sauce gets thick before the beef is tender, loosen it with a splash of broth or water.

**Rest the chicken, finish the sauce.** Move the chicken to a bowl and rest it 5 min. Meanwhile simmer the sauce uncovered, stir in the slurry, and cook 1 to 2 min until it coats a spoon. Add the lime juice, then taste and adjust the salt. You should have about 3 1/2 cups. Set aside 1 cup in a small pot to keep warm for the finish.

**Pull the beef, finish the sauce.** Move the beef to a bowl and heat the oven to 400°F. Skim any fat off the sauce, then simmer it uncovered, stir in the slurry, and cook 1 to 2 min until it coats a spoon. Add the lime juice, then taste and adjust the salt. You should have about 3 1/2 cups. Add broth if you are short. Set aside 1 cup in a small pot to keep warm for the finish.

**Shred and make the filling.** Shred the chicken while still warm, using two forks pulling with the grain, or a hand mixer or stand mixer paddle on low for 20 to 30 sec. Stop when no big chunks remain. Toss with the beans, corn, and 1/2 cup of the sauce. This is the filling. It stays in the bowl and does not go back into the pot.

**Shred and make the filling.** Shred the beef while still warm with two forks, pulling out any fat or gristle. Toss with the beans, corn, and 1/2 cup of the sauce. This is the filling. It stays in the bowl and does not go back into the pot.

**Shred and make the filling.** Shred the beef while still warm with two forks, pulling out any gristle. Toss with the beans, corn, and 1/2 cup of the sauce, plus 1/4 cup from the reserved finishing sauce, since eye of round shreds drier. This is the filling. It stays in the bowl and does not go back into the pot.
**Warm the tortillas.** Wrap the stack in a damp towel and microwave 45 to 60 sec. Keep them wrapped until you build.

**Layer.** Spread 1/2 cup of sauce over the bottom of the dish. Dunk each tortilla in the sauce quickly, then cut or tear it in half and lay the halves with the straight edge against the side of the dish. Halves cover the rectangle far more easily than whole rounds. Build two identical layers and a top layer.
   - Layers 1 and 2 (identical): 4 tortillas (8 halves), with torn pieces filling any gaps. Then 1/3 of the filling, half the cottage cheese, 1/2 oz cheese, and about 1/3 cup of sauce spooned over.
   - Top layer: 4 tortillas (8 halves), the last 1/3 of the filling, and about 1/3 cup of sauce. No cottage cheese or cheese inside. Hold the last 4 oz of cheese back.
   - Sauce budget, about 3 1/2 cups total: 1/2 cup in the filling, 1/2 cup on the bottom of the dish, about 1/2 cup picked up by the dunking, 1 cup over the three layers, and 1 cup held back for the finish. If you run short, thin the sauce with a splash of broth.
**Bake covered.** Tent with foil, keeping it off the surface, and bake at 400°F for 20 min.

**Top and crisp.** Uncover, scatter the remaining 4 oz of cheese, and bake 8 to 10 min until bubbling at the edges. Broil 1 to 2 min, watching the whole time, until the cheese browns in spots. In a Pyrex dish, skip the broiler and run the oven at 425°F for the last few minutes instead.
**Rest 10 min** so the layers set, then cut into 6. Spoon the warm reserved sauce over the cheese on each portion and top with scallions and pickled jalapeños, with lime wedges on the side.

notes.body: The traditional row assumes 1.5 lb of 80/20 beef, 12 tortillas fried in about 3 tbsp of oil, canned sauce, 8 oz of cheese, and 1/2 cup of sour cream. The fat savings come from the lean meat, the dry-warmed tortillas, less cheese, and cottage cheese in place of sour cream. They go toward protein and the beans and corn, so carbs run higher than the traditional version. Fat lands around 25% with chicken, 27% with eye of round, and 34% with chuck. The toppings and pickled jalapeños are not counted (the whole jar of pickles is about 25 cal).

**Shredded chicken**

- **Even pieces, bare simmer.** Thick ends overcook while thin ends dry out, and a hard boil turns the breast stringy
- **Pull at 165°F.** Past that point the breast loses moisture it won't get back
- **Shred warm and sauce it right away.** Cold breast crumbles into dry shards, and warm shreds soak up the sauce that keeps them juicy through the bake. A hand mixer on low does 1.5 lb in under a minute

**Shredded beef**

- **Lowest simmer, covered.** A hard boil dries the outside before the inside goes tender
- **Go by the fork, not the clock.** It is done when a chunk falls apart with no pull. Undercooked beef shreds into tough strings
- **Shred warm and sauce it right away.** The collagen sets as it cools, and warm shreds soak up the sauce
**Cook the meat in the sauce.** The meat seasons the sauce and the sauce seasons the meat, with no separate cooking step or extra fat

**Bloom the spice mix, but not the sweet paprika.** A minute in the hot oil takes the gritty edge off the chili powder. Sweet paprika scorches brown and bitter in a dry pan, so it goes in with the liquids to keep the sauce red
**Warm the tortillas, then dunk them in the sauce.** Cold corn tortillas crack, and the sauce dip is what replaces the fry oil
**Top cheese after the covered bake, finishing sauce after that.** Under foil or under sauce the cheese steams instead of crisping
**Chicken dry or stringy:** it boiled or went past 165°F. Toss the shreds with more sauce or a splash of broth, and hold a bare simmer next time
**Beef tough or dry:** tough means it needs more time, so keep braising and check every 20 min. Dry means it ran too hot or uncovered, so toss the shreds with more sauce
**Soggy casserole:** the sauce was too thin or the filling was wet. Thicken the sauce until it coats a spoon and drain the beans and corn harder
**Sauce brown instead of red:** the spices scorched in the bloom or the paprika went in too early. Keep the bloom to 1 min over medium and add the paprika with the liquids
**Sauce too sharp or salty:** a pinch more brown sugar for sharp, more lime for salty
**More cheese:** each extra ounce adds about 1.5g fat per serving. With chicken, 6 oz lands at about 27% fat. For 6 oz, use 1 oz inside each of the two layers instead of 1/2 oz and keep 4 oz on top
**Lower carb:** the tortillas, beans, and corn are all carb sources. Dropping to two layers of 4 tortillas cuts about 8g carbs per serving
**More protein:** an extra half pound of chicken adds about 9g protein per serving for about 1g fat
